Relative risk ratios

Source: R/qoi.R
rrr.Rd

Exponentiated coefficients of a choice model: for an alternative-specific coefficient \(\beta_{jm}\), \(e^{\beta_{jm}}\) is the factor by which a unit increase in covariate \(m\) multiplies the odds of alternative \(j\) relative to the base (Stata's mlogit, rrr); for a generic coefficient it multiplies the odds of any alternative relative to any other per unit of the alternative-specific covariate; for the split equation it multiplies the odds of the choice regime (logit link only).

Usage

rrr(object, level = 0.95)

Arguments

object

A "choicemodel" fit.

level

Confidence level for the (Wald, exponentiated) interval.

Value

A data frame with term, block, rrr, lower, upper, and the z statistic and p-value of the underlying coefficient.

Details

The odds reading holds for the multinomial logit, the inflated multinomial logit (whose outcome stage is a multinomial logit within the choice regime), and the random-intercept multinomial logit, where it is conditional on the unit's intercepts (the population-averaged odds ratio is closer to one). It does not hold for the nested logit (within a nest the ratio is \(e^{\beta/\lambda}\), across nests it is not constant), the HEV model (the odds depend on the scales), or the multinomial probit, so rrr() refuses those fits: use first_difference().

See also

first_difference(), summary.choicemodel()

Other quantities of interest: first_difference()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- rmnl(800, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5)))
rrr(mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d))
#>           term   block   rrr lower upper      z  p.value
#>  b:(Intercept) outcome 1.752 1.443 2.127  5.671 1.42e-08
#>           b:x1 outcome 0.374 0.299 0.467 -8.649  < 2e-16
#>           b:x2 outcome 2.030 1.653 2.492  6.763 1.35e-11
#>  c:(Intercept) outcome 0.840 0.664 1.064 -1.447    0.148
#>           c:x1 outcome 1.637 1.303 2.056  4.234 2.29e-05
#>           c:x2 outcome 0.632 0.511 0.781 -4.241 2.23e-05
